sentences.en: A storm of political controversy swirls around Kennedy on visit thousands expected to greet JFK.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪访问期间，政治争议的阴云笼罩，预计成千上万的人将迎接肯尼迪总统。

sentences.en: Dallas police said Thursday night they anticipate that thousands of welcomers will jam Love Field to greet President Kennedy when his jet airliner lands there Friday morning.
sentences.zh: 达拉斯警方周四晚表示，他们预计周五上午肯尼迪总统的喷气式客机降落时，成千上万的欢迎者将挤满爱田机场迎接他。

sentences.en: Ed Reynolds, president of the Dallas Retail Merchants Association, urged owners and tenants of Main Street buildings to fly the U.S.
sentences.zh: 达拉斯零售商协会主席埃德·雷诺兹敦促主街建筑的业主和租户悬挂美国国旗。

sentences.en: flag.
sentences.zh: 国旗。

sentences.en: He said the association also arranged for overhead decorations.
sentences.zh: 他说，协会还安排了高空装饰。

sentences.en: Former Vice President Richard Nixon, who ran against President Kennedy in 1960, joined police in urging Dallas residents to give President and Mrs. Kennedy a courteous reception.
sentences.zh: 曾在1960年与肯尼迪总统竞选的前副总统理查德·尼克松，与警方一起敦促达拉斯居民给予总统和肯尼迪夫人礼貌的接待。

sentences.en: Nixon, who was in Dallas for a meeting of soft drink bottlers, said discourteous groups harm their own cause and help their opponents.
sentences.zh: 尼克松当时正在达拉斯参加软饮料装瓶商会议，他说无礼的团体只会损害他们自己的事业，并帮助他们的对手。

sentences.en: One anti-Kennedy faction scattered leaflets which condemned the President for his stand on integration.
sentences.zh: 一个反肯尼迪派系散发了传单，谴责总统在种族融合问题上的立场。

sentences.en: President Kennedy will ride in a blue convertible.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪总统将乘坐一辆蓝色敞篷车。

sentences.en: If rain is falling, a plexiglass bubble will protect him.
sentences.zh: 如果下雨，有机玻璃罩将保护他。

sentences.en: The specially built car was flown here for use in the motorcade.
sentences.zh: 这辆特制的汽车被空运到这里，用于车队巡游。

sentences.en: Police said the motorcade will move slowly so that crowds can get a good view of President Kennedy and his wife.
sentences.zh: 警方表示，车队将缓慢行驶，以便人群能清楚地看到肯尼迪总统和他的妻子。

sentences.en: That, Dominic, was the Dallas Morning News on Friday, the 22nd of November 1963.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，那段话出自1963年11月22日星期五的《达拉斯晨报》。

sentences.en: It is, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Never has it been read in such a remarkable accent, I have to say, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我不得不说，这段话读起来口音真是非同寻常。

sentences.en: There was a definite hint of Wiltshire there, I think, as much as of Dallas.
sentences.zh: 我觉得里面既有达拉斯的味道，也有明显的威尔特郡口音。

sentences.en: I wasn't trying to be Dallas.
sentences.zh: 我并不是想模仿达拉斯口音。

sentences.en: I was trying to kind of multi-purpose, cheery 1960s US newscaster, and I think I hit the spot there.
sentences.zh: 我只是想扮演一个多功能的、欢快的1960年代美国新闻播音员，我想我抓住了精髓。

sentences.en: Do you think so?
sentences.zh: 你觉得呢？

sentences.en: That's good.
sentences.zh: 那很好。

sentences.en: It's good that you think it's anywhere.
sentences.zh: 你能觉得它像什么地方都好。

sentences.en: Well, we're talking of hitting the spot.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们正在谈论抓住精髓。

sentences.en: Well, there's a lot of ironies there, aren't there?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这里面有很多讽刺意味，不是吗？

sentences.en: There's a lot of ironies in that article.
sentences.zh: 那篇文章里有很多讽刺之处。

sentences.en: The fly in the US flag.
sentences.zh: 美国国旗上的苍蝇。

sentences.en: The presence of Richard Nixon.
sentences.zh: 理查德·尼克松的出现。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Who has just been in Dallas for a meeting of soft drink bottlers.
sentences.zh: 他刚好在达拉斯参加软饮料装瓶商会议。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Urging a courteous reception.
sentences.zh: 敦促给予礼貌的接待。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the police saying the motorcade will move slowly so the crowds can get a good view of President Kennedy and his wife.
sentences.zh: 还有警方说车队会缓慢行驶，这样人群就能清楚地看到肯尼迪总统和他的妻子。

sentences.en: And kind of the grim, macabre irony of that is one that no one needs explaining.
sentences.zh: 那种阴森、可怕的讽刺意味，根本不需要解释。

sentences.en: Because the events of Friday, the 22nd of November 1963 are so iconic that pretty much everyone knows about it.
sentences.zh: 因为1963年11月22日星期五发生的事件太具标志性了，几乎每个人都知道。

sentences.en: And I have to say, Dominic, you recommended that I read Parkland by Vincent Bugliosi.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我不得不说，你推荐我读文森特·布格里奥西写的《帕克兰》。

sentences.en: Which is one of the most gripping history books that I've ever read.
sentences.zh: 这是我读过的最引人入胜的历史书之一。

sentences.en: Twinkie.
sentences.zh: 特温基。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: It's a kind of blow by blow, almost minute by minute account of everything that happens on the day of Kennedy's assassination and the days that follow.
sentences.zh: 它几乎是逐分钟地记录了肯尼迪遇刺当天及随后几天发生的一切。

sentences.en: And what I found when I was reading it, it's a bit like kind of reading Hamlet for the first time.
sentences.zh: 我在阅读时发现，这有点像第一次读《哈姆雷特》。

sentences.en: Where you're aware of all the quotations, but you don't quite know how they fit in.
sentences.zh: 你知道所有的名言，但不太清楚它们是如何衔接在一起的。

sentences.en: And likewise, I had a sense of grassy knolls and Jack Ruby and book dispensaries and things like that.
sentences.zh: 同样，我对草丘、杰克·鲁比、教科书仓库之类的事情也有所耳闻。

sentences.en: But you read it and you thread it all together and you realize that this is one of the great primal narratives now of history.
sentences.zh: 但当你读完并把它们串联起来时，你会意识到这是现代历史上最伟大的原始叙事之一。

sentences.en: It is absolutely modern history.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是现代历史。

sentences.en: Certainly, it's become a foundational myth for modern America.
sentences.zh: 当然，它已经成为现代美国的奠基神话。

sentences.en: The moment of lost innocence, hasn't it?
sentences.zh: 那是失去纯真的时刻，不是吗？

sentences.en: And you mentioned that Bugliosi book.
sentences.zh: 你提到了布格里奥西的那本书。

sentences.en: So I reviewed that for the Daily Telegraph, I think, about 15 years ago.
sentences.zh: 我想大约15年前，我为《每日电讯报》写过书评。

sentences.en: And it had a different title then.
sentences.zh: 那时它的书名不同。

sentences.en: It was called Four Days in November.
sentences.zh: 它叫《十一月的四天》。

sentences.en: And it has a really interesting history because actually it's quite a long book, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 它的历史非常有趣，因为实际上这是一本很长的书，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But it is merely a fragment of a much longer book he wrote called Reclaiming History, which is this enormous survey, not just of the events of the day,
sentences.zh: 但这仅仅是他所写的一本更长著作《重申历史》的片段，那是一项巨大的调查，不仅涵盖了当天的事件，

sentences.en: but a biography of Lee Harvey Oswald and an absolutely forensic investigation of all the conspiracy theories surrounding Kennedy's assassination.
sentences.zh: 还包括李·哈维·奥斯瓦尔德的传记，以及对围绕肯尼迪遇刺的所有阴谋论的绝对法医式调查。

sentences.en: So it's an extraordinary, extraordinary book.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一本非常、非常了不起的书。

sentences.en: And Bugliosi himself is a remarkable man because he was the prosecutor of Charles Manson.
sentences.zh: 布格里奥西本人也是个了不起的人，因为他是查尔斯·曼森的检察官。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Of the Manson murders in the late 1960s.
sentences.zh: 1960年代末曼森谋杀案的检察官。

sentences.en: Helter Skelter.
sentences.zh: 《混乱》。

sentences.en: Helter Skelter was his book about the case.
sentences.zh: 《混乱》是他关于那个案件的书。

sentences.en: And Dominic, can I just ask, I am not in any way an expert in this at all, as listeners will already have gauged.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我能问一下吗？正如听众们已经察觉到的，我完全不是这方面的专家。

sentences.en: To what extent does Bugliosi's book hold up?
sentences.zh: 布格里奥西的书在多大程度上站得住脚？

sentences.en: Is it widely recognized as authoritative or does it have lots of critics still to this day?
sentences.zh: 它被广泛认为是权威的吗？还是说至今仍有许多批评者？

sentences.en: First of all, if you look on Amazon, you'll find loads of disobliging reviews of it.
sentences.zh: 首先，如果你在亚马逊上查看，会发现大量对其不以为然的评论。

sentences.en: It's very unpopular with people in what you might call the conspiracy community or people who are sympathetic to the conspiracy theories.
sentences.zh: 它在所谓的阴谋论圈子或同情阴谋论的人群中非常不受欢迎。

sentences.en: So a lot of people will say he goes too far in trying to sort of sow the conspiracy theorists' fields with salt.
sentences.zh: 所以很多人会说，他在试图用盐播种阴谋论者的田地方面走得太远了。

sentences.en: The other thing, I mean, we were talking about this, weren't we, off air in the last few days.
sentences.zh: 另一件事是，我们过去几天在节目外也谈论过这个，不是吗？

sentences.en: The Kennedy assassination is not a subject that academics write about, that academic scholars write about.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪遇刺案并不是学术界研究的主题，学术学者们并不写这个。

sentences.en: So there's very little, as it were, scholarly literature on the Kennedy assassination.
sentences.zh: 所以关于肯尼迪遇刺案的学术文献非常少。

sentences.en: Because it's like Atlantis or aliens.
sentences.zh: 因为它就像亚特兰蒂斯或外星人一样。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It is seen as a sort of Graham Hancock-shaped hole into which you will fall and you'll never climb out again.
sentences.zh: 它被视为一个格雷厄姆·汉考克式的深坑，一旦掉进去就永远爬不出来。

sentences.en: And you'll find yourself in this weird sort of hall of mirrors.
sentences.zh: 你会发现自己置身于一个奇怪的镜厅之中。

sentences.en: And it doesn't really play a part in any kind of, you know, scholarly conversations about 20th century America.
sentences.zh: 它在关于20世纪美国的任何学术对话中并没有真正发挥作用。

sentences.en: I think because people are frightened of it because they think it's, you know, the stuff of UFOs.
sentences.zh: 我想是因为人们害怕它，因为他们认为这是UFO之类的东西。

sentences.en: And as you say, ancient Atlantis and the Yeti and all that business.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，古代亚特兰蒂斯、雪人等等那一套。

sentences.en: And yet, I mean, it is very, very historically significant, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 然而，它在历史上确实非常、非常重要，不是吗？

sentences.en: As a foundational episode in modern America, as you said, but also as an expression of powerful themes in American history.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，它是现代美国的奠基事件，也是美国历史上强大主题的表达。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: All the anxieties about the Kennedy assassination.
sentences.zh: 所有关于肯尼迪遇刺案的焦虑。

sentences.en: The anxieties about an overreaching government.
sentences.zh: 对权力过度扩张的政府的焦虑。

sentences.en: About corrupt conspirators.
sentences.zh: 关于腐败的阴谋者。

sentences.en: About an establishment that rigged things to suit themselves.
sentences.zh: 关于一个为了自身利益而操纵一切的建制派。

sentences.en: All of those kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 所有这些事情。

sentences.en: But also, of course, it opens up windows into the tumult about civil rights in the early 1960s.
sentences.zh: 当然，它也打开了了解1960年代初民权运动动荡的窗口。

sentences.en: About Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 关于越南。

sentences.en: Yeah, the rise of the new conservatism in opposition to the sort of top-down establishment liberalism.
sentences.zh: 是的，反对自上而下的建制派自由主义的新保守主义的兴起。

sentences.en: Vietnam, as you say.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，越南。

sentences.en: Cold War.
sentences.zh: 冷战。

sentences.en: Cuba.
sentences.zh: 古巴。

sentences.en: All of these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 所有这些事情。

sentences.en: So, Dominic, all the themes, essentially, that we were kind of touching on in our previous episode, where we looked at the achievements or non-achievements of Kennedy's presidency.
sentences.zh: 所以，多米尼克，基本上就是我们在上一集探讨肯尼迪总统任期的成就或非成就时所触及的所有主题。

sentences.en: But you brought us to Texas in November 1963.
sentences.zh: 但你把我们带到了1963年11月的德克萨斯州。

sentences.en: And so, perhaps now we should dive in deep and look at the events of his trip to Texas.
sentences.zh: 所以，也许现在我们应该深入探讨他德克萨斯之行的事件。

sentences.en: Because you said that Parkland was originally called Four Days in November.
sentences.zh: 因为你说《帕克兰》最初叫《十一月的四天》。

sentences.en: And that was the name of a film that was released in 1964.
sentences.zh: 那也是1964年发行的一部电影的名字。

sentences.en: It was nominated for an Oscar as Best Documentary.
sentences.zh: 它曾获得奥斯卡最佳纪录片提名。

sentences.en: And I watched that last night.
sentences.zh: 我昨晚看了那部片子。

sentences.en: I hadn't realized that actually Kennedy had gone to Florida beforehand.
sentences.zh: 我之前没意识到肯尼迪在那之前还去了佛罗里达。

sentences.en: Yes, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: He was making a general kind of southern trip.
sentences.zh: 他当时正在进行一次南方之行。

sentences.en: To shore up his base.
sentences.zh: 为了巩固他的基本盘。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: As we said last time, if you listened to our podcast last week about Kennedy's early life and then his road to the presidency and his presidency,
sentences.zh: 正如我们上次所说，如果你听了我们上周关于肯尼迪早年生活、通往总统之路以及总统任期的播客，

sentences.en: Kennedy in November 1963 is looking forward to the election a year later.
sentences.zh: 1963年11月的肯尼迪正期待着一年后的大选。

sentences.en: He has the best approval ratings that anyone has ever had.
sentences.zh: 他拥有有史以来最好的支持率。

sentences.en: And on the other hand, as with all democratic presidents, his re-election depends upon him preserving a coalition of kind of northern cities and industrial states and the,
sentences.zh: 另一方面，正如所有民主党总统一样，他的连任取决于他能否维持一个由北方城市、工业州和，

sentences.en: up to this point, solidly democratic South.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，铁杆民主党的南方组成的联盟。

sentences.en: But his support for civil rights in the summer of 1963 has imperiled his coalition in the South.
sentences.zh: 但他对1963年夏天民权运动的支持已经危及了他在南方的联盟。

sentences.en: So it makes sense for him to do this little southern tour a year out from the election to show his face, you know, do all the airport photo calls.
sentences.zh: 所以他在大选前一年进行这次小规模的南方巡回访问是有意义的，露露面，你知道，做所有的机场拍照活动。

sentences.en: Taking Jackie with him will bring greater publicity because he knows how popular she is and how much people are excited to see her.
sentences.zh: 带上杰基会带来更大的宣传效应，因为他知道她有多受欢迎，人们有多兴奋见到她。

sentences.en: And this is her first trip with him since 1960 on a kind of trip like this.
sentences.zh: 这是她自1960年以来第一次陪他进行这样的旅行。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But also, crucially, it's her first trip since the tragic loss of their baby son, Patrick, who had died, I think, two days after being born in AuguSt.
sentences.zh: 但至关重要的是，这也是她自他们的小儿子帕特里克不幸夭折后的第一次旅行，我想他在八月出生两天后就去世了。

sentences.en: And this had been a devastating moment for both of them.
sentences.zh: 这对他们俩来说都是一个毁灭性的时刻。

sentences.en: They have two children already, John Jr.
sentences.zh: 他们已经有两个孩子了，小约翰。

sentences.en: and Caroline.
sentences.zh: 和卡罗琳。

sentences.en: She had gone into a deep depression, but people said it had kind of brought them closer together.
sentences.zh: 她曾陷入深深的抑郁，但人们说这反而让他们更加亲密了。

sentences.en: So they are making the trip together.
sentences.zh: 所以他们一起踏上了旅程。

sentences.en: It is a kind of special moment for them.
sentences.zh: 这对他们来说是一个特殊的时刻。

sentences.en: So as you say, Tom, they've been in Florida on Thursday, the 21st of November.
sentences.zh: 所以正如你所说，汤姆，他们在11月21日星期四去了佛罗里达。

sentences.en: Kennedy, of course, doesn't know it, but he has a day to live.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪当然不知道，但他只剩下最后一天生命了。

sentences.en: They fly into Texas.
sentences.zh: 他们飞往德克萨斯州。

sentences.en: They go to San Antonio.
sentences.zh: 他们去了圣安东尼奥。

sentences.en: They meet up with Vice President Johnson and his wife, Lady Bird Johnson.
sentences.zh: 他们会见了副总统约翰逊和他的妻子伯德夫人。

sentences.en: They go to Houston for a dinner.
sentences.zh: 他们去休斯顿参加了一场晚宴。

sentences.en: And then very late at night, so about 11 o'clock, they arrive in Fort Worth, which is Dallas.
sentences.zh: 然后很晚的时候，大约11点，他们抵达了沃斯堡，也就是达拉斯。

sentences.en: It's kind of sister city.
sentences.zh: 那是姐妹城市。

sentences.en: They're effectively one metropolis.
sentences.zh: 它们实际上是一个大都市区。

sentences.en: They get into the hotel very late.
sentences.zh: 他们很晚才住进酒店。

sentences.en: It's going to be a busy day the next day, so they go straight to bed.
sentences.zh: 第二天会很忙，所以他们直接上床睡觉了。

sentences.en: And JFK doesn't have the best suite, does he?
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪住的不是最好的套房，对吧？

sentences.en: That goes to LBJ because the Secret Service are worried it's not secure enough.
sentences.zh: 那是给林登·约翰逊的，因为特勤局担心那里的安保不够严密。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: He has a decent suite.
sentences.zh: 他住的套房还不错。

sentences.en: He's in the Texas Hotel in Fort Worth.
sentences.zh: 他住在沃斯堡的德克萨斯酒店。

sentences.en: He doesn't sleep in the same bedroom as Jackie.
sentences.zh: 他没有和杰基睡在同一个卧室。

sentences.en: That's very common.
sentences.zh: 这很常见。

sentences.en: You know, he's obviously going to be working late often.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他显然经常工作到很晚。

sentences.en: She won't want to go to bed earlier.
sentences.zh: 她不想睡得太早。

sentences.en: That's sort of fairly standard.
sentences.zh: 这算是相当标准的。

sentences.en: And they've got a very busy day lined up.
sentences.zh: 他们安排了非常忙碌的一天。

sentences.en: The plan for Friday the 22nd of November is there will be a breakfast event in Fort Worth at the hotel when they'll have local business leaders from Fort Worth.
sentences.zh: 11月22日星期五的计划是，沃斯堡酒店将举行早餐活动，届时会有沃斯堡当地的商界领袖参加。

sentences.en: They will then fly to Dallas.
sentences.zh: 然后他们将飞往达拉斯。

sentences.en: We'll talk about the flight in a second.
sentences.zh: 我们一会儿再谈这次飞行。

sentences.en: They'll fly to Dallas.
sentences.zh: 他们将飞往达拉斯。

sentences.en: He will go through the streets of Dallas in a motorcade, which you talked about in that
sentences.zh: 他将乘坐车队穿过达拉斯的街道，也就是你在那篇《达拉斯晨报》剪报中提到的内容。

sentences.en: Dallas Morning News clipping.
sentences.zh: 《达拉斯晨报》剪报。

sentences.en: He will speak to Dallas business leaders at the Trademart that's just outside Dallas's downtown to the south.
sentences.zh: 他将在达拉斯市中心以南的贸易中心向达拉斯的商界领袖发表演讲。

sentences.en: And then he will go on to Austin, Texas for an evening fundraiser.
sentences.zh: 之后他将前往德克萨斯州的奥斯汀参加一场晚间筹款活动。

sentences.en: And then he's going to go on to LBJ's ranch, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 然后他要去林登·约翰逊（LBJ）的牧场，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He's going to rest at LBJ's ranch.
sentences.zh: 他打算在LBJ的牧场休息。

sentences.en: And then on Saturday, the next day, he will go back to Washington.
sentences.zh: 接着在第二天，也就是周六，他将返回华盛顿。

sentences.en: And the big thing they're looking forward to is their son, John Jr.'s third birthday on Monday.
sentences.zh: 他们最期待的大事是周一他们儿子小约翰的三岁生日。

sentences.en: It's very important to them.
sentences.zh: 这对他们来说非常重要。

sentences.en: They're back for John Jr.'s birthday.
sentences.zh: 他们是为了小约翰的生日回来的。

sentences.en: Oh, dang.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: It's just the shadows of tragedy over here are awful.
sentences.zh: 这里的悲剧阴影真是太可怕了。

sentences.en: Well, there's a human story here.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这背后有一个人性化的故事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There are multiple human stories that are so often forgotten amid the swirl of conspiracy paranoia and stuff.
sentences.zh: 在阴谋论和偏执的喧嚣中，有许多人性化的故事往往被人们遗忘了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So let's go on to Friday and let's take this kind of-
sentences.zh: 那么让我们回到周五，让我们把这当作一种——

sentences.en: Play by play.
sentences.zh: 逐场比赛的解说。

sentences.en: Like detectives piling up the evidence.
sentences.zh: 就像侦探们在堆积证据一样。

sentences.en: Let's pile up the evidence.
sentences.zh: 让我们来堆积证据吧。

sentences.en: Kennedy awakes at about 7.30 in the morning.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪在早上7点半左右醒来。

sentences.en: As you said, Tom, he's not in the best suite.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，汤姆，他住的并不是最好的套房。

sentences.en: He's on the eighth floor.
sentences.zh: 他在八楼。

sentences.en: He has a black man servant called George Thomas who often goes in to wake him.
sentences.zh: 他有一位名叫乔治·托马斯的黑人侍从，经常进去叫醒他。

sentences.en: And George Thomas puts out his suit and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 乔治·托马斯会帮他准备好西装之类的东西。

sentences.en: They don't get much peace.
sentences.zh: 他们得不到多少安宁。

sentences.en: You don't get much sort of solitude if you're the president of the United States because they've
sentences.zh: 如果你是美国总统，你就很难有那种独处的时光，因为他们

sentences.en: got all this huge entourage and they've got all this colossal amount of equipment that they take with them.
sentences.zh: 带着庞大的随行人员，还有随身携带的大量笨重设备。

sentences.en: It's a phone, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 那是部电话，对吧？

sentences.en: So he can reach anywhere in the world at any time.
sentences.zh: 这样他就能随时随地联系到世界上的任何地方。

sentences.en: He's meant to be never more than five minutes away from this crucial network that will plug him into the White House switchboard and mean that he can reach.
sentences.zh: 他被要求必须随时处于这个关键网络五分钟的覆盖范围内，这个网络能让他接通白宫总机，意味着他可以联系到任何人。

sentences.en: If he wanted to call you, Tom- He could do it.
sentences.zh: 如果他想给你打电话，汤姆——他随时都能做到。

sentences.en: He could do it.
sentences.zh: 他确实能做到。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So he gets up.
sentences.zh: 所以他起床了。

sentences.en: Jackie is still asleep.
sentences.zh: 杰奎琳还在睡觉。

sentences.en: The description of him getting up is actually a fascinating insight into the health problems that we talked about last week.
sentences.zh: 关于他起床的描述，实际上让我们深入了解了我们上周谈到的健康问题。

sentences.en: So he has been sleeping on a sort of board that he has, a special bed board, which goes with him wherever he goes for his back, which is destroyed.
sentences.zh: 他一直睡在一种他特有的木板上，一种特殊的床板，无论去哪儿他都带着，因为他的背部已经毁了。

sentences.en: He puts on this back brace, this sort of stiff corset type thing.
sentences.zh: 他穿上这种背部支架，一种僵硬的紧身胸衣之类的东西。

sentences.en: This will be important, won't it?
sentences.zh: 这很重要，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: When the events happen, the role of that.
sentences.zh: 当事件发生时，它的作用（很重要）。

sentences.en: And Dominic, again, just to name check the Four Days in November, the documentary I saw, there is a sequence of him getting into his car in Florida and the look of pain on
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，再次提一下那部纪录片《十一月的四天》，我看到过一个片段，他当时在佛罗里达上车，他坐下时

sentences.en: his face as he sits down, really, really vivid.
sentences.zh: 脸上的痛苦表情，真的非常非常生动。

sentences.en: And also kind of throw away comment from a journalist, a reporter saying about, you know, you could see his tan from five miles away.
sentences.zh: 还有一位记者随口评论说，你知道，你在五英里外就能看到他的晒痕。

sentences.en: And he's got that tan, hasn't he?
sentences.zh: 他确实晒得很黑，不是吗？

sentences.en: Principally to cover up kind of the marks of pain and illness that he's got on his face.
sentences.zh: 主要是为了掩盖他脸上痛苦和疾病的痕迹。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He's a good example of somebody who, because he's in such horrendous health, actually almost overcompensates by presenting a portrait of kind of glowing good health at all times.
sentences.zh: 他是一个很好的例子，因为他身体状况极差，实际上通过时刻展现出一副容光焕发的健康形象来过度补偿。

sentences.en: But the tan also helps him to disguise the fact that he's taking the cocktail of drugs.
sentences.zh: 但晒黑也有助于他掩盖自己正在服用混合药物的事实。

sentences.en: He has Addison's disease.
sentences.zh: 他患有阿狄森氏病。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He has suffered with fever ever since World War II.
sentences.zh: 自二战以来，他一直饱受发烧的折磨。

sentences.en: So the tan helps to cover up the fact that he would otherwise look very sallow and kind of yellow.
sentences.zh: 所以晒黑有助于掩盖他本来会显得非常苍白和蜡黄的肤色。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So yes, he goes through this great operation of getting ready.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，他经历了这一整套准备工作。

sentences.en: It's now about eight o'clock and there are 5,000 people downstairs in the parking lot of the hotel.
sentences.zh: 现在大约是八点钟，楼下的酒店停车场里有5000人。

sentences.en: And many of them have been waiting for three hours or so to see him.
sentences.zh: 他们中许多人已经等了三个小时左右，就为了见他一面。

sentences.en: So actually, the granular detail gives you a sense of the demands on any public figure in the early 1960s.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，这些细致入微的细节让你感受到了20世纪60年代初公众人物所面临的要求。

sentences.en: And especially a president.
sentences.zh: 尤其是总统。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He has given his news briefing for the day.
sentences.zh: 他已经完成了当天的简报会。

sentences.en: There's very little news.
sentences.zh: 其实没什么新闻。

sentences.en: Actually, the fact that one of the leading items in the news briefing is a Labour Party victory in the Dundee West by-election in Britain, Tom.
sentences.zh: 事实上，简报会上的头条新闻之一竟然是英国工党在邓迪西选区补选中获胜，汤姆。

sentences.en: Labour winning by-elections in Scotland, whatever next.
sentences.zh: 工党在苏格兰赢得了补选，接下来还会发生什么呢。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But the big news in the press is twofold.
sentences.zh: 但媒体报道的大新闻有两点。

sentences.en: First of all, as we talked about last time, there was terrible faction fighting within the Texas Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 首先，正如我们上次谈到的，德克萨斯州民主党内部存在严重的派系斗争。

sentences.en: He won Texas by, what, 46,000 votes or something in 1960.
sentences.zh: 他在1960年以46000票左右的优势赢得了德克萨斯州。

sentences.en: So not many.
sentences.zh: 所以优势并不大。

sentences.en: He needs the Texas Democratic Party to be united.
sentences.zh: 他需要德克萨斯州民主党团结一致。

sentences.en: The feud between Governor Connolly and Senator Yarbrough, so on the relatively conservative,
sentences.zh: 康纳利州长和亚伯勒参议员之间的不和，分别代表了党内相对保守和

sentences.en: relatively liberal wings of the party, respectively, that's a problem and he has to fix it.
sentences.zh: 相对自由的派系，这是一个问题，他必须解决它。

sentences.en: That's part of what this trip to Dallas is all about.
sentences.zh: 这就是这次达拉斯之行的部分目的。

sentences.en: But the other big thing is about his reception.
sentences.zh: 但另一件大事是关于他受到的接待。

sentences.en: Now, you mentioned Nixon saying he hoped that Kennedy would get a courteous reception.
sentences.zh: 你提到了尼克松说他希望肯尼迪能受到礼貌的接待。

sentences.en: Dallas, in particular, has a reputation as being a difficult place to visit.
sentences.zh: 达拉斯尤其以一个难以访问的地方而闻名。

sentences.en: So Lyndon Johnson, who is from Texas, had been spat at during the 1960 presidential campaign.
sentences.zh: 所以林登·约翰逊，这位来自德克萨斯州的人，在1960年总统竞选期间曾被人吐过口水。

sentences.en: More pertinently, Kennedy's predecessor is the kind of democratic standard bearer, Adlai Stevenson, who's now his ambassador to the United Nations.
sentences.zh: 更贴切地说，肯尼迪的前任，民主党的旗手阿德莱·史蒂文森，也就是他现在的联合国大使。

sentences.en: He had actually been hit with a placard and spat at less than a month earlier.
sentences.zh: 就在不到一个月前，他被人用标语牌打了，还被吐了口水。

sentences.en: And the Secret Service, I gather, had recorded 34 threats on the president's life from Texas between 1961 to 62.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，特勤局记录了1961年到1962年间来自德克萨斯州针对总统生命的34次威胁。

sentences.en: So Kennedy kind of knows what he says, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 所以肯尼迪心里有数，不是吗？

sentences.en: Oh, we're heading into nut country today.
sentences.zh: 噢，我们今天要进入疯子窝了。

sentences.en: He does indeed.
sentences.zh: 他确实知道。

sentences.en: So Dallas has this reputation as a hotbed of conservatism.
sentences.zh: 所以达拉斯有保守主义温床的声誉。

sentences.en: It's a very business-friendly town.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常商业友好的城市。

sentences.en: It's a town with, you know, a lot of people who are suspicious of the federal government.
sentences.zh: 这里有很多人对联邦政府持怀疑态度。

sentences.en: Obviously, civil rights has ignited a power keg among a lot of white Southerners.
sentences.zh: 显然，民权问题已经在许多南方白人中点燃了火药桶。

sentences.en: You know, there have been leaflets out on the streets with Kennedy's face on saying, wanted for treason, all of this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，街上到处都是印着肯尼迪头像的传单，上面写着“因叛国罪被通缉”，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: Now, the interesting thing is that how much are we focusing on these things because they're unusual
sentences.zh: 现在，有趣的是，我们关注这些事情是因为它们不寻常，

sentences.en: or how much are we focusing on them because we know Kennedy is going to be assassinated?
sentences.zh: 还是因为我们知道肯尼迪即将被暗杀？

sentences.en: In the 1950s and 1960s, it was very common to see leaflets and pamphlets and things like that making strident, wild political claiMs.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪50年代和60年代，看到传单、小册子之类的东西发表尖锐、疯狂的政治主张是非常普遍的。

sentences.en: So this is the heyday of the far-right John Birch Society.
sentences.zh: 那是极右翼约翰·伯奇协会的全盛时期。

sentences.en: Obviously, the Ku Klux Klan is still kind of going strong in parts of the South.
sentences.zh: 显然，三K党在南方部分地区依然活跃。

sentences.en: There are inflamed passions and have been for a considerable time.
sentences.zh: 人们的情绪一直很激动，而且已经持续了相当长一段时间。

sentences.en: I mean, it's not that long since McCarthyism.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，麦卡锡主义过去并没有多久。

sentences.en: So there are lots of people, I mean, not a majority, of course, by any means, but there are people who will say Kennedy is a communiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以有很多人，当然不是大多数，但确实有人会说肯尼迪是共产主义者。

sentences.en: You know, there are people who think Eisenhower's a communiSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，还有人认为艾森豪威尔是共产主义者。

sentences.en: So the fact that there are leaflets and the fact that there are people who are possibly going to heckle him, that's not something he's unused to.
sentences.zh: 所以有传单，有人可能会对他起哄，这对他来说并不陌生。

sentences.en: You know, that is part of the territory in early 60s America.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是60年代初美国政治环境的一部分。

sentences.en: But there does seem to have been, and maybe this is retrospective, but I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 但似乎确实存在一种不安感，也许这是事后回顾，但我不这么认为。

sentences.en: There does seem to have been a particular jumpiness around this trip.
sentences.zh: 这次行程周围似乎确实有一种特别的紧张感。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The plan is what?
sentences.zh: 计划是什么？

sentences.en: That he's going to drive nine and a half miles in a motorcade past very high-rise buildings.
sentences.zh: 他将乘车队行驶九英里半，经过非常高大的建筑物。

sentences.en: I mean, people in the security service are twitchy about this, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，安保部门的人对此感到紧张，对吧？

sentences.en: They are.
sentences.zh: 他们确实很紧张。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course they are.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然了。

sentences.en: They know that Kennedy, he likes to put himself into the crowds.
sentences.zh: 他们知道肯尼迪喜欢深入人群。

sentences.en: He likes to stop and greet people.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢停下来和人们打招呼。

sentences.en: That all of that glad-handing is part of his style.
sentences.zh: 所有这些亲民举动都是他风格的一部分。

sentences.en: And it's the security service's job to try and intercept these things.
sentences.zh: 而安保部门的工作就是试图阻止这些事情。

sentences.en: Somebody had tried to shoot Roosevelt in the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 20世纪30年代曾有人试图枪杀罗斯福。

sentences.en: Every year there are death threats against American presidents.
sentences.zh: 每年都有针对美国总统的死亡威胁。

sentences.en: So, of course, they are anxious.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们当然会感到焦虑。

sentences.en: I guess they're confident that they can handle it.
sentences.zh: 我想他们有信心能处理好。

sentences.en: Otherwise, they wouldn't be doing the motorcade at all.
sentences.zh: 否则他们根本就不会进行车队游行。

sentences.en: But that morning is all going very well, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但那天早上一切都很顺利，不是吗？

sentences.en: The breakfast meeting in the Grand Ballroom goes tremendously.
sentences.zh: 大宴会厅的早餐会进行得非常棒。

sentences.en: Kennedy does his bounce.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪表现得很有活力。

sentences.en: Jackie turns up a bit late because she's been titivating, and she turns up in her pink Chanel suit.
sentences.zh: 杰奎琳因为在梳妆打扮迟到了一点，她穿着那套粉红色的香奈儿套装出现了。

sentences.en: And Kennedy kind of jakes that in Paris he'd been introduced as the guy who accompanies Mrs. Kennedy.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪开玩笑说在巴黎他被介绍为“陪同肯尼迪夫人的那个人”。

sentences.en: And it's much the same thing in Texas.
sentences.zh: 在德克萨斯州也是一样的情况。

sentences.en: And there's much horseplay with a Stetson hat.
sentences.zh: 还有很多关于牛仔帽的玩笑。

sentences.en: There is, but he doesn't put it on.
sentences.zh: 确实有，但他没有戴上它。

sentences.en: He doesn't want to put it on.
sentences.zh: 他不想戴上它。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And then he gets given a pair of cowboy boots to guard against the rattlesnakes at LBJ's ranch.
sentences.zh: 然后他被赠予了一双牛仔靴，以防范LBJ牧场里的响尾蛇。

sentences.en: So it all seems to be going tremendously well.
sentences.zh: 所以一切看起来都进行得非常顺利。

sentences.en: It does go well.
sentences.zh: 确实进行得很顺利。

sentences.en: This goes very well.
sentences.zh: 这进行得非常顺利。

sentences.en: And as you say, Jackie, I mean, how can she possibly know that when she puts on that outfit that morning, which is this very elegant pink Chanel suit with a pillbox hat,
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，杰奎琳，我的意思是，当她那天早上穿上那套衣服时，那套非常优雅的粉色香奈儿套装配上药盒帽，她怎么可能知道

sentences.en: that that is the outfit with which she'll be forever associated.
sentences.zh: 那将是她永远被联系在一起的装束。

sentences.en: It ends up being splattered with her husband's blood.
sentences.zh: 它最终被她丈夫的鲜血溅满了。

sentences.en: Anyway, they did the Fort Worth event.
sentences.zh: 总之，他们完成了沃斯堡的活动。

sentences.en: That's all great.
sentences.zh: 一切都很棒。

sentences.en: They go back upstairs.
sentences.zh: 他们回到楼上。

sentences.en: They've got a few moments before they have to go.
sentences.zh: 在离开之前他们还有一点时间。

sentences.en: So they go back up to the suite.
sentences.zh: 所以他们回到了套房。

sentences.en: And it's actually when he's in the suite that his aide, Ken O'Donnell, shows him the Dallas Morning News.
sentences.zh: 实际上，正是在套房里，他的助手肯·奥唐奈向他展示了《达拉斯晨报》。

sentences.en: And the Dallas Morning News that morning is carrying a full page advertisement with a funereal kind of black border.
sentences.zh: 那天早上的《达拉斯晨报》刊登了一则带有葬礼般黑色边框的全版广告。

sentences.en: It says, welcome, Mr. Kennedy to Dallas.
sentences.zh: 上面写着：欢迎肯尼迪先生来到达拉斯。

sentences.en: Now, this ad is going to be very important later on for Jack Ruby.
sentences.zh: 现在，这则广告后来对杰克·鲁比来说非常重要。

sentences.en: So listeners should kind of make a note of this.
sentences.zh: 所以听众应该记下这一点。

sentences.en: The ad says that it's been placed by something called the American Fact Finding Committee, chaired by one Bernard Weissman.
sentences.zh: 广告称它是由一个叫“美国事实调查委员会”的组织投放的，主席是伯纳德·魏斯曼。

sentences.en: And it says, it has 12 questions for Kennedy.
sentences.zh: 上面写着，它有12个问题要问肯尼迪。

sentences.en: And the 12 questions are basically, why are you supporting communist policies?
sentences.zh: 这12个问题基本上是：你为什么要支持共产主义政策？

sentences.en: Why do the communists rejoice in all your achievements?
